newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK FIN MIN CLARIFIES TAX ON INTERBANK DEALS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK FIN MIN CLARIFIES TAX ON INTERBANK DEALS.

text.p: Net interest income from interbank deals will be taxed at the corporate tax rate for banks, the Greek finance ministry said in a statement issued to clarify renewed confusion on the subject.

"Concerning the issue of taxing interest on interbank loans, as referred to in chapter four of the introductory page of the 1997 budget (page 91, number 22), it is clarified that the tax will be implemented according to the procedure announced by the government on November 20," the statement said.
Net interest income from interbank deals from January 1 will be taxed as other types of income, it said. The actual method of tax calculation will be explained in the upcoming tax bill.
In applying the new law, banks will have to prepay 60 percent of their taxes, a rise from 50 percent previously, it said.
The budget was apparently mistaken in saying a withholding tax of 20 percent would be applied to interest on interbank loans. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
